name: tsa_createOtp
description: Stores a new OTP hash for a phone number, valid for 10 minutes, after marking every unused OTP for that number as used. The Next.js caller generates the 6-digit code, hashes it with SHA-256 and sends the plaintext by SMS (Twilio); the plaintext never reaches the database. Currently unused while the app runs the tsa_loginByPhone bypass. Called by the TSA Eats Next.js app (tsa-eats/lib/api.ts) through api/Endpoints/TsaApi.cs, which maps queryType 'createOtp' to [TSA].[tsa_createOtp]. There is no Harrier Central auth: POST requires the shared X-Api-Key (TsaApiKey); GET requires nothing, and the shim does not restrict which procedure a GET may name. The shim turns any one-row rowset with Success = 0 into HTTP 400 {success:false, errorMessage}, and an empty first rowset into HTTP 404.

parameters.name: otpHash
parameters.description: SHA-256 hex hash of the 6-digit code. No default.

rowsets.name: SuccessEnvelope
rowsets.description: Success or CATCH error, one row.

columns.name: ErrorMessage
columns.description: NULL on success; ERROR_MESSAGE() on error.

sideEffects: UPDATE TSA.OtpCode SET usedAt = now for the phone's unused codes.
INSERT TSA.OtpCode (one row, expiresAt = now + 10 minutes).

codeSmells.detail: @phoneNumber, @otpHash (lines 2-3) have no SQL default. A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the body runs: no log row, and the TsaApi shim returns a generic 500.
The CATCH (lines 35-38) returns the error envelope but writes nothing to HC.ErrorLog or any TSA log table, so failures are only visible in Azure Function logs as a 400 warning.
Nothing limits how often a code can be requested for a number; each call is an SMS sent by the caller.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
